note: A CHAMBER RED THAT gate-commit STRUCTURALLY CANNOT CATCH, and the number that explains it. The Legend bounced from the chamber with rc=11 on the gate phase after 470s. Locally make gate-commit was rc=0. Both are true and neither is a bug: gate-commit runs the SUB-FLOOR TIER ONLY, and the failing test was not in docs/timings/subfloor-roster.tsv (verified, zero matches), so it had never once run on this branch. The chamber gate phase runs the full workspace suite: 4882 tests against gate-commit 983. CLAUDE.md states this division plainly, that coverage is the stage gate job and not the commit gate one, and I still read a green gate-commit as though it were coverage. SECOND TRAP, and it is the one that nearly caused a second bounce: the chamber report said recorded 1 failing test. THAT MEANS AT LEAST ONE, NOT EXACTLY ONE. Running the suite locally with --no-fail-fast found FOUR. An agent then labelled three of them pre-existing and unrelated; git log --diff-filter=A showed the file containing two of them was CREATED BY THIS CAMPAIGN three commits earlier, and the third failed because this campaign own change made a golden stale. All three were ours. Fixing only the reported one would have bounced us again, costing the whole queue a second serial slot. THIRD, the root cause behind all of it: this branch never absorbed main in eleven tasks, so main moved 593 COMMITS before the first submission. That single omission billed three times — a 593-commit absorption, a 470s chamber red, and three of our own tests broken by genesis drift the absorption carried in. Two of those three had been FLAGGED IN THEIR OWN TASK REPORT as pinned to hardcoded seed-35 geometry that a future genesis change could move. It did. THE CHEAP PREVENTION IS make sluice-stage: it runs the same four phases against the same real merge product, its refusal is free, and it leaves main untouched by construction. It costs a queue slot, not a merge. Run it at every plan-stage boundary; a green gate-commit is not evidence about the full suite and never was.
